newsitem.title: UK: Gilts end flat, unable to hold higher ground.
newsitem.headline: Gilts end flat, unable to hold higher ground.

text.p: 1625 GMT - Gilts ended little changed having reached giddy heights more than a half-point above Friday's close. That could not be sustained and the market fell back. Now, it is awaiting Tuesday's PSBR followed by unemployment and retail sales on Wednesday. * March gilt future settled 1/32 higher at 109-02
U.S. industrial output, released at 1415 GMT, rose 0.9 percent in November. Economists had forecast a 0.6 percent rise and the Treasury market wobbled.
Gilts, meanwhile, had dropped to a session low of 108-29, down 4/32 on the day.
"When we fell back and went into the red, buyers emerged," the salesman said.

Now, the market will look to Tuesday's PSBR figures for November. A 2.7 billion stg shortfall is forecast but after the previous month's bumper repayment of 4.4 billion stg, the market is fairly sanguine about Britain's public finances.
"The PSBR is not a real worry. The government's targets are credible," said Tom Rayner, economist at Societe Generale.
In his November budget, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke forecast at 1996/97 PSBR of 26.4 billion stg, falling to 19.2 billion the following year.

Wednesday's retail sales and unemployment data should also pass without to much incident. A steady 0.5 percent increase in sales volume is forecast in November while unemployment is expected to fall by about 25,000 with annual average earnings growth holding steady at 4.0 percent.
"It would take a huge jobless fall or average earnings to rise to really shake gilts and I don't expect either," the salesman said.
Nonetheless, gilts are unlikely to outperform their major European counterparts.

"We expect continuing underperformance from our market but I wouldn't expect to see 200 on the spread unless the future gets down to 108-08," the salesman said. "And both those marks would represent powerful reasons to buy again."
The gilt/Bund spread stood at 191 basis points late on Monday.

The March and June short sterling futures both settled unchanged at 93.45 and 93.20 respectively. That profile discounts a total of 75 basis points in interest rate rises by the middle of next year. Base rates are now at six percent.
